newsitem.title: USA: HitCom to buy telecom company stake.
newsitem.headline: HitCom to buy telecom company stake.

text.p: HitCom Corp said Tuesday it signed a letter of intent to buy 80 percent of the stock of One Plus Marketing Inc, an Illinois corporation that provides telephone and Internet access services.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Based on fully diluted outstanding shares following the One Plus transaction, HitCom said it projects its 1997 earnings per share will be between $0.20 and $0.25 per share.
HitCom said it is completing an audit and will report 1996 financial results during March.

One Plus Marketing, which began operating in 1994, had 1995 revenue of $500,000 and 1996 revenue of $2 million, with 1996 profit of more than $500,000. The company is projecting revenue of $4 million to $4.5 million in 1997, said One Plus president Scott Bell.

"Our acquisition of One Plus completes a series of strategic transactions that puts us squarely in three core businesses, each of which has excellent growth potential," said HitCom chairman Anthony Hitt.
HitCom recently completed the acquisition of Technology Solutions Inc, a Salt Lake City-based computer computer training company.

Brian Creath, president of HitCom's IntelliSource subsidiary, said the company intends to enter the Internet service provider business and link this business to its existing IntelliPages business and soon to be launched IntelliSource Service.
HitCom, a marketing and technology company, recently completed a one-for-four reverse stock split. Hitt said the company is seeking to become a fully reporting NASDAQ company during March or April.
